details:
Beyond the Mission: NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars

Team Name: MISSION12

Beyond the Mission is an educational and interactive storytelling project focused on equipment left behind by space missions on the Moon and Mars. Space exploration leaves behind various objects, including landing systems, spacecraft components, rover-related hardware and scientific instruments. These objects tell important stories about humanity's journey into space, but their history is often overlooked.

Our project proposes an interactive digital platform where users can explore the Moon and Mars through 3D visualisations, discover locations of equipment left behind by past missions, and learn about the history, purpose and reasons behind each object. We highlight real missions such as Apollo 11, Mars Pathfinder, Curiosity and Perseverance to connect users with actual space exploration history.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Our project aims to make space exploration more engaging, educational and accessible. It helps people understand the history of past missions, discover the equipment they left behind, and learn why responsible and sustainable space exploration matters. We hope to inspire curiosity about space and encourage greater awareness of humanity's impact on other planetary surfaces.

Tools and Technology:

We used Canva to design our presentation and develop our project website. We also used Cesium as our 3D visualisation technology reference. Cesium can help create interactive 3D environments where users can explore planetary surfaces and visualise mission locations. Our proposed platform would combine this visualisation technology with NASA mission information. We have not developed custom code or used specialised hardware for this project.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of our project is its storytelling approach. Instead of focusing only on famous space missions and their discoveries, we explore the often-overlooked equipment they leave behind. We transform these objects into educational stories, allowing users to understand the journeys, engineering and history behind them.

Factors Considered:

Our team considered educational value, accessibility, accuracy of mission information, ease of exploration and responsible space exploration. We also considered how 3D visualisation could make complex space information easier to understand and more interesting for users.

Through Beyond the Mission, we aim to turn forgotten mission equipment into a journey through humanity's exploration of space.
